text:
Anna Lopez: Heads up — proposing a tweak to the default canary fallback ordering. Current platform default is model-variant -> capacity -> region. I'm suggesting we flip capacity and region so the order becomes model-variant -> region -> capacity for multi-region customers. Short rationale and a config example below. Thoughts? @Miles @Rashid :thinking_face:

Miles Chen: Curious — what's the primary driver? latency or cost? Region-first could add egress and cross-region latency for write-heavy apps.

Anna Lopez: Both. My thinking: for customer-facing apps where regulatory locality matters (EU-only, etc.) and session affinity is important, regional failover preserves locality and legal constraints. Capacity fallback (spill to other SKUs/tiers) can be more expensive and should be last resort.

Rashid Patel: We need clear metrics to trigger each. Proposal:
- error_rate_delta > 1.5x for 1m -> model-variant fallback
- p99_latency increase > 200ms for 30s -> regional failover
- queue_depth > 80% for 60s -> capacity fallback
Also add a fast-succession guard to avoid flip-flopping.

Kevin O'Connor: +1 on metrics. Also add tenant tier override: enterprise tenants can pin region-first, dev orgs use cost-first (capacity).

Aly (devx): UX question — how do we expose this in Console? A simple dropdown for "Fallback priority" with presets (Balanced / Locality-first / Cost-first) + an advanced editor for thresholds. We should show expected egress delta and cost estimate for the chosen preset.

Anna Lopez: Yep. Console should show a simulation preview based on recent traffic (last 24h) to estimate how often each fallback would trigger.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary rollout v3.2 -> v3.3, 5% traffic, region us-west-2, time=1782567890

Miles Chen: Concern — automatic region failover: what about stateful backends (session KV)? If we move region, KV misses will spike. Need fallback to degrade to read-only mode or sticky sessions.

Rashid Patel: Agreed. Add a precondition check: state_miss_rate < 5% for region failover. If >5% then skip to capacity fallback.

Anna Lopez: Good point. Revised heuristic (summary): model-variant fallback (safety) -> regional failover (if locality + state preconditions) -> capacity fallback (scale to other pools). Fast flip guard: once a tenant fails over, don't attempt another failover for X minutes unless severity > critical.

Kevin O'Connor: For alerts/telemetry, we should emit a structured event when a fallback occurs with fields: tenant_id, fallback_type, reason_code, pre_metrics, post_metrics, duration. That helps dashboards and incident triage.

Aly (devx): Example console notification text for a regional failover: "Automatic regional failover triggered for tenant acme-corp due to P99 latency spike (+260ms). Traffic routed to eu-west-1. Estimated cost delta +12% until recovery." We can link to the rollback button and a "force pin to region" action.

Anna Lopez: Here's a minimal policy YAML I sketched for the runtime engineers: 

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  priority: [model_variant, region, capacity]
  guards:
    model_variant:
      error_ratio_threshold: 1.5
      window_seconds: 60
    region:
      p99_latency_increase_ms: 200
      window_seconds: 30
      state_miss_rate_threshold: 0.05
    capacity:
      queue_depth_pct: 80
      sustained_seconds: 60
  flip_guard_seconds: 600
  tenant_overrides:
    enterprise:
      priority: [model_variant, region, capacity]
    dev-tier:
      priority: [model_variant, capacity, region]
```

Rashid Patel: Looks good. One more: include a cool-down multiplier for retry backoff so noisy networks don't oscillate.

deploy-bot: canary traffic update: 10% -> 20% after 15m (auto-scale check passed)

sre-bot: log: [1782568012] tenant=acme-corp fallback=region reason=p99_latency pre_p99=480ms post_p99=120ms duration=00:03:40

sre-bot: log: [1782568240] tenant=acme-corp revert=auto reason=stabilized duration=00:03:28

Miles Chen: Nice — those logs will be super useful. Can we make the logs stream to a per-tenant timeline in Console and allow replay of decision path?

Aly (devx): Yes, decision-path replay is doable: timeline + arrows showing rule matches and metric snapshots. We'll mock a UI for next week.

Anna Lopez: Thanks all — next steps:
1) Eng runtime: implement priority/guards as config + flip_guard and state precondition checks
2) Telemetry: emit structured fallback events and timeline entries
3) Devex: Console presets + simulation + decision replay mock
4) SRE: add logs/alerting for fallback churn

Kevin O'Connor: I'll own telemetry schema. Rashid + Miles help with thresholds. Anna and Aly coordinate Console UX.

Aly (devx): I'll drop a mock in #design by EOD Friday. :rocket:

Anna Lopez: Thanks — tagging this for the weekly rollouts sync. :thumbsup:

Miles Chen: :+1:

Rashid Patel: LGTM

Kevin O'Connor: ACK
